q.intro.text: A class keeps a record of five students and their birthday months. Each arrow goes from a student to the month of their birthday.

q.ask.text: The record can be read two ways: student to month, or month to student. Which way is a function?

e.intro.text: Four steps. Press each one: the diagram moves first, then the board.

e.s1.text: The inputs are the students: every arrow starts at one. A function gives every input exactly one output.

e.s2.text: Follow each student's arrows. Ava to March, Ben to July, Cara to March, Dev to October, Eli to May. Every student has exactly one arrow.

e.s3.text: Ava and Cara share March. That is allowed: no student has two months. So student to month is a function.

e.s4.text: Now flip it: month to student. March has two arrows, to Ava and to Cara. One input with two outputs, so month to student is not a function.

e.why.text: Quick check: why is student to month a function, even though March is used twice?

e.w-ok.text: Yes. The test is about the inputs: each student needs exactly one month. Two students may share one.

e.w-oto.text: A function does not need different outputs. What it forbids is one input with two outputs.

e.w-first.text: Every arrow counts, not just the first. Here each student happens to have only one arrow.

t.intro.text: Now a relation on a graph. Each point is a pair: input, output. The first step is done for you.

t.s1.text: The five points as pairs: negative three, two. Negative one, negative two. One, three. Three, two. And one, negative four. The board lists them.

t.slice.text: Your step: a vertical slice fixes one input and meets all its outputs. Which input has two points on its slice?

t.sl-ok.text: Yes: the slice at x equals one meets one, three and one, negative four.

t.sl-shared.text: The points at negative three and three are at the same height: they share an output. Each of those slices meets only one point.

t.sl-other.text: The slice at x equals negative one meets only one point. Look for a slice that meets two.

t.share.text: Your step: negative three, two and three, two share the output two. Does that break the function?

t.sh-ok.text: Right: inputs may share an output. That is allowed, and it is not what breaks this relation.

t.sh-no.text: Sharing an output is allowed: negative three and three each still have exactly one output.

t.wit.text: Last step: which sentence proves that this is not a function?

t.w-ok.text: Yes: one input with two outputs, quoted from the graph. That is a counterexample, and one is enough.

t.w-out.text: The output two having two inputs is allowed. The proof needs an input with two outputs.

t.w-vague.text: True, but a proof names where: the input one, with the outputs three and negative four.

t.cb-right.text: At the start you picked student to month only, and you were right: each student has one month, but March has two students.

t.cb-month.text: At the start you picked month to student. That checks the outputs. A function is checked from the inputs, and as an input March has two students.

t.cb-both.text: At the start you picked both. Flipping can break a function: as an input, March goes to two students.

t.cb-sure.text: You were sure, and changing your mind after being sure is exactly how this sticks.

p.intro.text: Jordan says: y equals x squared is not a function, because two and negative two both give four.

p.j-ok.text: Jordan is wrong. Now prove it: fill each because with the reason that makes the line true.

p.j-test.text: Let's test it. Build the argument and see where it leads.

p.c1.text: Each input x gives exactly one value of x squared,

p.c2.text: and two and negative two sharing the output four is allowed,

p.c3.text: so y equals x squared is a function, and Jordan is wrong.

p.x-line.text: Curves can be functions. What matters is one output for each input.

p.x-examples.text: A few checks cannot cover every input. The reason has to work for every x.

p.x-other.text: True, but it is the reason for a different line.

p.done.text: That's a proof: an argument about every input, plus a shared output that is allowed. y equals x squared is a function.
